title: Pyramid Transition Matrix Problem

notes: The order of the first two characters in each allowed pattern is significant.
A solution may use different valid upper rows; finding one complete construction is sufficient.
constraints: The letters in all input strings are from the set {'A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'}.
All the values of allowed are unique.

content.problemStatement:
You are stacking blocks to form a pyramid. Each block has a color, which is represented by a single letter. Each row of blocks includes **one less block** than the row beneath it and is centered on top.

To make the pyramid aesthetically pleasing, there are only specific **triangular patterns** that are allowed. A triangular pattern is composed of a **single block** stacked on top of **two blocks**. The patterns are given as a list of three-letter strings `allowed`, where the first two characters of a pattern represent the left and right bottom blocks respectively, and the third character is the top block.

* As an example, `"ABC"` represents a triangular pattern with a `'C'` block stacked on top of an `'A'` (left) and `'B'` (right) block. Keep in mind that this is different from `"BAC"` where `'B'` is on the left bottom and `'A'` is on the right bottom.

You start with a bottom row of blocks `bottom`, given as a single string, that you **must** use as the base of the pyramid.

With `bottom` and `allowed`, output `true` *if you can build the pyramid all the way to the top such that **every triangular pattern** in the pyramid is in* `allowed`*, or* `false` *otherwise*.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/08/26/pyramid1-grid.jpg)

```
Input: bottom = "BCD", allowed = ["BCC","CDE","CEA","FFF"]
Output: true
Explanation: The allowed triangular patterns are shown on the right.
Starting from the bottom (level 3), we can build "CE" on level 2 and then build "A" on level 1.
There are three triangular patterns in the pyramid, which are "BCC", "CDE", and "CEA". All are allowed.
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/08/26/pyramid2-grid.jpg)

```
Input: bottom = "AAAA", allowed = ["AAB","AAC","BCD","BBE","DEF"]
Output: false
Explanation: The allowed triangular patterns are shown on the right.
Starting from the bottom (level 4), there are multiple ways to build level 3, but trying all the possibilites, you will get always stuck before building level 1.
```

**Constraints:**

* `2 <= bottom.length <= 6`
* `0 <= allowed.length <= 216`
* `allowed[i].length == 3`
* The letters in all input strings are from the set `{'A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'}`.
* All the values of `allowed` are **unique**.

notes: All advertised implementations read the same JSON argument line and emit a JSON-compatible boolean.
There are only 36 possible ordered base-pairs because the alphabet has six colors.
Memoization must distinguish ordered pairs: AB and BA can have different allowed tops.
solution.approach: Index each ordered pair of neighboring colors to all allowed top colors, then use depth-first search to build each possible upper row. Memoize rows that are proven impossible so the same intermediate row is never recomputed. The search succeeds as soon as any sequence reaches a one-block row.

better.complexity: Still exponential in the number of reachable row states, with O(n) work per explored row and no memoization.
better.description: Pre-index allowed by the ordered bottom pair so each pair lookup is constant-time, then recursively generate upper rows. This removes repeated scans of the allowed list but still recomputes the same upper rows.

optimal.complexity: O(n * 6^n) time and O(6^n) auxiliary space in the worst case for n <= 6.
optimal.description: Use DFS with pair-to-top adjacency lists and memoize every row that cannot reach the top. For each row, recursively enumerate its possible next row; when a generated row has length one, the construction is complete.

bruteForce.complexity: Worst case exponential in the number of cells above the bottom; using the six-color alphabet, the number of possible full assignments is bounded by O(6^(n(n-1)/2)).
bruteForce.description: Enumerate every possible pyramid construction directly, checking each triangular pattern against allowed. This repeats identical intermediate rows many times.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n * 6^n) in the worst case for n = bottom.length, with at most 6 possible colors per position and memoization across reachable rows.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(6^n) for memoized failed rows, plus O(n) recursion and working-row construction.

followUps: How would the search change if the alphabet contained more than six colors?
Can you rewrite the recursive search iteratively while preserving memoization?
What changes would be needed if the bottom row length were much larger than six?
